claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO introduces additional phonon-scattering centers.
The additional scattering from SRO disrupts the coherence of vibrational modes.
Scattering introduced by SRO outweighs any reduction in mass-disorder scattering caused by ordering.
The initial disordered alloy has high configurational entropy.
The constituent elements of the initial alloy have significant mass and size mismatch.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce or enhance SRO without necessarily changing the nominal composition.
Compositional tuning can promote local atomic clustering or ordering.
At temperatures below the Debye temperature, phonon-phonon scattering is dominant in the proposed system.
External magnetic or electric fields can alter phonon dispersion.
SRO clusters produce local deviations in bonding environments and interatomic force constants.
These local deviations act as distinct scattering centers for mid-to-long-wavelength phonons.
SRO produces local force-constant and mass variations distinct from those of a fully random alloy.
The SRO-associated variations introduce Rayleigh-like phonon-scattering channels.
The additional scattering reduces the phonon mean free path.
An SRO-enhanced sample will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than a chemically identical disordered sample.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity suppression will correlate with the measured degree of SRO.
Coherent precipitates formed during SRO-promoting treatment could act as ballistic heat-transport channels and invalidate the expected suppression.
SRO may enhance vibrational coherence when its length scale becomes comparable to the phonon mean free path.
Ordering-dominated behavior is less likely in refractory alloys.
